## Quarto

`use_excalidraw_slides()` copies the `excalidraw` Quarto extension into a
folder and adds a demo deck:

```{r}
library(excalidrawer)
use_excalidraw_slides("talk")
```

```bash
quarto render talk/slides.qmd
```

The deck uses `format: excalidraw-revealjs`, which brings:

- Excalifont headings and text, Excalidraw's colours, sketchy code blocks and
  callouts;
- figures sized for slides, drawn with ragg so the handwriting fonts appear;
- `excalidraw: paper:` in the YAML for `dots`, `graph`, `lines`, `kraft`,
  `blueprint` or `chalkboard` paper;
- sticky notes: `[Remember to smile]{.sticky-note}` (also `.blue`, `.pink`,
  `.green`);
- boxes with a rough border: `::: {.sketch-box}` (add `data-fill="#a5d8ff"`
  for a hachure fill);
- hand-drawn marks on words: `[word]{.rn-underline}`, `.rn-circle`,
  `.rn-box`, `.rn-highlight`, `.rn-strike`, `.rn-cross`, `.rn-bracket`. Add
  `.fragment` to draw a mark on click.

In R chunks, print `sketch()` objects or `plot()` scenes. Use
`background = FALSE` to let the paper show through.

```{r}
sketch(p, background = FALSE)
as_excalidraw(p) |> exc_note("look!", x = "suv", y = 50) |> plot(background = FALSE)
```

Print the rendered deck to PDF (one slide per page) with headless Chrome:

```{r}
exc_slides_pdf("talk/slides.html")
```

## PowerPoint

`exc_pptx()` writes one slide per chart, scene, or Excalidraw frame. Drawings
are placed as editable vector shapes:

```{r}
exc_pptx(list(p, s), "talk.pptx", titles = c("What people drive", "SUVs win"))
```

Text is drawn as shapes by default so it looks right on any computer. For
editable text, use `text = "font"` and install the fonts where PowerPoint can
find them:

```{r}
exc_install_fonts()
exc_pptx(s, "editable.pptx", text = "font")
```

A scene made of Excalidraw frames becomes a deck with one slide per frame,
titled with the frame names, so you can lay out slides on an Excalidraw canvas
and export them.
